text: Where ForEach repeats over a fixed collection, the Until activity provides exactly what a do-until loop provides in any real programming language. It runs its child activities repeatedly until an expression actually evaluates true, with no fixed number of iterations known in advance at all.

That expression gets evaluated after every single pass through the child activities, not before. If it's false, the loop runs its child activities again. The moment it evaluates true, the Until activity completes — a common pattern checks a variable's current value against whatever finished genuinely looks like.

Select Edit Activities to add whatever the loop should actually run each pass — often a Wait activity paired with something that checks status, and a Set Variable activity that updates the exact value the expression is watching. One real behavior worth knowing: if a child activity inside the loop fails, the Until activity genuinely doesn't stop — it keeps looping regardless.

Every Until activity carries a timeout, defaulting to seven full days if you don't set one yourself, with a real maximum of ninety days. Without a sensible timeout, a condition that never actually becomes true would otherwise loop essentially forever, silently consuming resources indefinitely.

A genuinely common real use: an external system processes something asynchronously, with no webhook telling you when it's actually done. An Until activity polls it directly — a Web activity checking status, a short Wait, repeated — until the status genuinely comes back complete, or a reasonable timeout gets hit. Next: the Execute Pipeline activity — one pipeline calling another, the pattern behind nested and parallel loops alike.
